1. The Moon is in synchronous rotation with Earth, meaning the same side (the near side) always faces our planet.
2. It likely formed about 4.5 billion years ago from debris after a Mars-sized body collided with the early Earth.
3. The Moon has no significant atmosphere, which leads to extreme temperature swings—from about 127°C (260°F) in sunlight to -173°C (-280°F) in darkness.
